premises.statement: A discipline reasons from its principles to conclusions without proving those principles.
Faith articles are principles of sacred doctrine.
An opponent may grant some revealed principles, or grant none.
Canonical Scripture is grounded in apostolic and prophetic revelation; authority of other doctors is probabilistic.
Philosopher authorities are extraneous probable arguments where natural reason knows a truth.
The objections cite claims about faith inquiry, human authority, and faith merit.

limitations: The source principles about revelation, infallibility, and canonical authority are not independently proven.
Conditional opponent-context cases establish only what follows from the stipulated grants; they do not prove revelation or infallibility.
No resurrection conclusion is inferred from an authority qualification alone; the resurrection example is inventoried as a source illustration requiring its own premise.
Native argumentation acceptance, baseline truth, and checker-reported properties remain distinct.
Full article verification is not claimed.
The objections and sed contra are text-only reconstructions; their source transitions are not executable in this profile.
source_derivation is a direct source-mapped case premise, not an independently derived proof step. available_argument reports conditional argument availability only.
The no-common-principle case supports only an answerable-objection result; it does not establish any faith article.
